title: Barrister Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to calculate a barrister salary from hourly rates using the 38-hour week, award rates, casual loading, and super paid on top. Fair Work Ombudsman figures included.
salarySummary: For a legal professional earning $36.03 per hour under the Legal Services Award, the annual salary is approximately $71,196 before tax and super, or $79,740 including 12% super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual barrister salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $36.03 per hour gives $36.03 × 38 × 52 = $71,196.48 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use the timesheet calculator on this site to do the conversion instantly.

faqs.q: Does the Legal Services Award cover barristers?
faqs.a: The Legal Services Award 2020 covers legal clerical and administrative employees, law graduates, and law clerks, but not self-employed barristers. Barristers typically negotiate their own fees. However, the award rates provide a useful benchmark for legal professionals. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets minimum rates for employees, while barristers’ income varies widely based on experience, caseload, and jurisdiction.

faqs.q: Is casual loading included in the hourly rate for barristers?
faqs.a: No. Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate for casual employees under awards. It compensates for leave entitlements. Barristers who are self-employed do not receive casual loading. If you are using the timesheet calculator, enter your base hourly rate and check the 'casual loading' box to add 25% – never enter a rate that already includes loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Barrister Salary from Hourly Rates

When discussing a **barrister salary**, it helps to start with the hourly rate. Whether you are a legal professional covered by an award or a self-employed barrister charging by the hour, converting an hourly figure to an annual amount gives you a clearer picture of your earnings. This guide uses the latest Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission data to show you how the conversion works, including the 38-hour week, casual loading, and superannuation paid on top.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours. So if you earn $36.03 per hour (the Law Clerk rate under the Legal Services Award from 1 July 2026), the calculation is:

$36.03 × 38 × 52 = $71,196.48 per year.

If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly figure. The timesheet on this site lets you enter any hours per week. Always assume the same rate every week – no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances are included in this estimate.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal floor. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. For legal professionals, the **Legal Services Award 2020** sets minimum pay for classifications such as:

- Level 1 Legal clerical: $28.24/hour
- Level 5 Law graduate: $33.99/hour
- Level 6 Law clerk: $36.03/hour 

A barrister salary is not directly set by this award because barristers are usually self-employed. But if you are an employee in a legal practice, these rates apply. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides summarise the award minimums.

### Casual Loading and How It Works

Casual employees under the Legal Services Award receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading replaces paid leave entitlements. For example, a casual law clerk would earn $36.03 + 25% = $45.04 per hour. The annual equivalent becomes $45.04 × 38 × 52 = $89,007.04.

**Important:** When using the timesheet calculator on this site, enter your base hourly rate only. Then check the “casual loading” box to add 25%. Do not type a rate that already includes loading. The calculator handles it correctly.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate – it is an additional cost for the employer.

For the law clerk example:
- Annual base: $71,196.48
- Super (12%): $8,543.58
- Total cost to employer: $79,740.06

If you are self-employed as a barrister, you may need to arrange your own super contributions. The Australian Taxation Office sets the rules for the super guarantee.

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Using the $71,196 annual salary, tax would be approximately:
- First $18,200 tax-free
- Next $26,800 at 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $26,196 at 30% = $7,858.80
- Total tax: $11,878.80
- Medicare (2% of $71,196) = $1,423.92
- Net pay: $71,196 – $11,878.80 – $1,423.92 = $57,893.28 per year, or about $1,113 per week.

This is an estimate. HELP loans, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted here.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the law clerk: $71,196.48 ÷ 26 = $2,738.33 per fortnight (before tax). The timesheet calculator shows both weekly and fortnightly figures.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

To calculate your own barrister salary or any hourly rate, visit [the timesheet](/). It lets you enter your base hourly rate, hours per week, and optionally add casual loading. The results show annual gross, super, tax, and net pay. For award rates and pay guides, see [pay guides](/blog). For detailed reference tables, check [reference tables](/data).

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
